subject: How to set memory limit in linux to get rid of killed job because of exceeding memory limit

messages.author: a2287a1bd46ca727
messages.subject: How to set memory limit in linux to get rid of killed job because of exceeding memory limit
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to use R/qtl on a linux server with several clusters as well as more than 128Go of memory but whatever the size of memory that I allocate to the job, I'm still getting my job killed when I run permutations with scantwo() because of exceeding memory limit.

I tried ulimit::memory_limit(128000) at the beginning of my script but I still get the same problem. Is there a way to limit the R usage of memory under linux OS to avoid job killing ?

Thanks

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: How to set memory limit in linux to get rid of killed job because of exceeding memory limit
parts:
I think you need to scale back on the number of permutations you are trying to do in one job, and maybe switch to the function scantwopermhk() which is more economical in its use of space. 

Can you say more about the data: number of markers, individuals, permutations, and whether you’re using covariates?

karl

messages.subject: Re: How to set memory limit in linux to get rid of killed job because of exceeding memory limit
parts:
Hi Karl,

My data contain around 250 individuals and 4000 markers. I would like to run 1000 permutations and I'm not using covariates nor stratified permutations.

I was trying to run 1000 permutations with scantwo(method="hk",n.cluster=N,n.perm=1000) in order to get the penalties needed to use the stepwiseqtl(additive.only=T) function.

I tried to allocate 128 to 256 Go and 25 to 50 cores (n.cluster) to my job without success.

Thanks for advising the scantwopermhk() function. However, it's not possible to use the "n.cluster" argument to parallelize the jobs isn't it ?

Justin

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: How to set memory limit in linux to get rid of killed job because of exceeding memory limit
parts:
scantwo permutations would be trying to create an object that's 4000 x 4000 x 1000, which is just too big.

The scantwopermhk() function behaves better, as it works with a chromosome pair at a time, rather than the full 4000x4000 matrix. But in any case you're likely going to want to split the 1000 permutations into multiple batches.

karl
